title: Tesla Schedules November Dallas Robotaxi Debut and 1M Unit Optimus Goal
summary:
The electric-car manufacturer will introduce an autonomous ride-hailing service in Texas to test scaling before a wider rollout, with expectations that the fleet will impact profits by early 2027. Tesla plans to launch Cybercab rides in Dallas in November 2026 and is targeting 24 hour operations by the end of that year. In Fremont, the company has installed production lines designed to build 1 million Optimus humanoid robots annually, while simultaneously expanding its Full Self-Driving software into nine European countries. Additionally, Tesla expects to produce its first test chips from the Austin Terafab in mid-2027.

These expansion goals follow Q3 results where free cash flow of $1.53 billion beat the projected $4.99 billion loss, and adjusted earnings per share hit $0.48 against a $0.44 estimate. Annual recurring revenue from autonomous subscriptions crossed $1 billion for the first time on 1.74 million users. CEO Elon Musk stated that vehicle demand currently exceeds production, leading to the largest passenger backlog in four years, and set a long-term target of 5 million vehicles per year by 2030. The company has also entered volume production of the Tesla Semi and nearly sold out its 2027 Megapack capacity.

selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
THE TESLA $TSLA SEMI IS NOW IN VOLUME PRODUCTION

The top version can go 500 miles fully loaded at 82,000 lbs, at an efficiency of 1.7 kWh per mile.

That means it uses about a third of the energy of a comparable diesel truck to haul the same load. In trucking, energy is one of the biggest costs per mile, so Tesla says that gives Semi operators a real advantage.

The Nevada factory is built for 25,000 Semis a year, and Tesla deployed its first pre-assembled Megacharger to support the ramp.

selectedTweets.text:
$TSLA - TESLA BEATS EARNINGS AS CASH FLOW SMASHES EXPECTATIONS

Tesla delivered a mixed Q3, but profitability and cash flow surprised sharply to the upside.

Adjusted EPS: $0.48 vs. $0.44 expected
Revenue: $28.05B vs. $28.13B expected
Gross margin: 19.6% vs. 17.8% expected
Free cash flow: +$1.53B vs. -$4.99B expected

FSD subscriptions surged to 1.74 million, while Optimus production began in Fremont.

The key takeaway: Strong margins, positive cash flow and accelerating FSD adoption offset a 56% decline in operating income.

Source: Tesla Q3 2026 Earnings
